standard_prerequisites.name: The regular-model situation, the degree pairing of the components and the genus of the curve
standard_prerequisites.statement: The situation fixes a discrete valuation ring, a smooth projective curve over its fraction field, a regular proper model and the components of the special fibre with their multiplicities; the degree pairing on combinations of components is symmetric and is computed from the degrees of the restrictions of the invertible sheaves attached to the components, and the genus of the special fibre can be read off from the numerical type and equals the genus of the curve. For a union of two effective Cartier divisors the structure sheaf fits into a short exact sequence comparing it with the sheaves of the parts, and the cohomology of the projective line over the residue field is known. The author's own lemmas of the chapter and the quoted results of the Divisors, Morphisms and Coherent chapters are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the constraint that keeps two minus-one curves from meeting in a general configuration, and it is used when minimal models are compared through sequences of contractions.

core_obligations: Set up the union of the two curves: since they meet, their union is an effective Cartier divisor on the regular surface, and the structure sheaf of the union fits into the exact sequence comparing it with the sheaves of the two components and of their intersection (source lines 4938-4950).

Compute the intersection number of the two curves: the degree pairing is symmetric, and evaluating the pairing on the two components gives their intersection number, which by the hypothesis is nonnegative and, since both curves are exceptional, enters the computation with the value one (source lines 4950-4965).

Compare genera: the genus of the curve equals the genus read off from the numerical type of the special fibre, and expressing that genus through the union and the components shows that the multiplicities must both be one and that the number of components is two (source lines 4965-4975).

Conclude the geometric assertions: the cohomology of the two components is that of the projective line over the residue field, the intersection point is rational, and the genus of the curve is zero, which are the remaining assertions of the statement (source lines 4975-4981).

proof_roadmap.step: Form the union of the two curves and write down the comparison exact sequence.
Compute the intersection number of the two exceptional curves through the degree pairing.
Compare the genus of the curve with the numerical type to force the multiplicities and the number of components.
Read off the projective-line structure, the rationality of the intersection point and the vanishing genus.
